newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says June drills unrelated to HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says June drills unrelated to HK handover.

text.p: Taiwan's defence ministry on Tuesday confirmed the island would hold its annual military exercises in late June, but said the timing had nothing to do with Hong Kong's scheduled July 1 return to China's rule.
The joint-forces' Han Kwang 13 drills would be held on June 23 and 24 in southern Tainan, Kaohsiung and Pingtung, the state-funded Central News Agency said.
"Although the exercises are held close to Hong Kong's handover to communist China, please do not link the two things together," the agency quoted a senior military officer as saying.
Local media have reported that the exercises would involve live-fire war games to allow troops to test new weapons purchased to counter China's military modernisation.

Media reports have said the exercises were designed to test a range of new high-technology systems, including new F-16 and Mirage fighters recently imported from the United States and France, despite Beijing's bitter objections, and newly refitted M60A3 tanks.
Also reportedly slated for testing were several French-made Lafayette-class frigates, nicknamed "stealth" warships because of their ability to evade radar.
In 1996, Taiwan suspended Han Kwang 12 drills to avoid exacerbating tensions with China after Beijing staged war games and missile tests near the island.
Taiwan resumed live-fire missile practice in March, test-firing U.S. Hawk missiles in the Taiwan Strait as military tensions with China abated.
China, which has regarded Taiwan as renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, vows to attack the island if it opts for independence.
